speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly when your double vision began and whether it affects both eyes or just one. Additionally, how would you describe the nature of your upper limb weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The worsening of your weakness with activity and improvement with rest is very characteristic of Myasthenia Gravis. Given your double vision, when does it typically occur during your day, and do you experience any difficulty swallowing or chewing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of diplopia that worsens with specific gaze and fatigable, symmetrical limb weakness is highly specific for this condition. I recommend a Tensilon test and acetylcholine receptor antibody levels to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR Antibody, Anti-MuSK Antibody.
